summary.en: Hear the future marker and the action as two parts.

body.en:
From season 1, episodes 1, 2, 4 and 6.

To talk about an ongoing or repeated action in the future, Russian combines a future form of **быть** (*to be*) with an imperfective infinitive: **сегодня ночью я буду спать спокойно** (*tonight I will sleep peacefully*) and **буду повторять всю дорогу** (*I will repeat it the whole way*).

Only **быть** changes for the person—**буду**, **будешь**, **будет**, **будем**, **будете**, **будут**—while the action verb stays in its infinitive (**спать**, **повторять**, **говорить**). To make it negative, put **не** right before the form of **быть**: **никто не будет говорить** (*nobody will talk*).

Keep in mind that Russian has a second future pattern for single completed results: in **отдадим сумку** (*we will hand back the bag*), the perfective verb expresses the future in one word without **будем**.

On replay, whenever you catch **буду** or **будет**, listen ahead for the infinitive that completes the thought—or if a noun or adjective follows instead, hear it simply as *will be*.
